questions.question: Which of the following is the natural source of acetic acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinegar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vinegar** is a liquid consisting of about **5-20% acetic acid** (ethanoic acid), water, and other trace chemicals, which may include flavorings.
 
• **Acetic acid** is produced by the **fermentation** of ethanol or sugars by **acetic acid bacteria** (Acetobacter family).
 
• It is widely used in **food preservation**, particularly in **pickling** processes, and as a common condiment in various cuisines.
 
• Chemically, acetic acid is represented by the formula **CH3COOH** and is a **weak acid** that gives vinegar its characteristic **sour taste** and **pungent smell**.
 
• While found in very small quantities in some fruits, **vinegar** is the concentrated natural source commonly associated with acetic acid in daily use. ***Hence, the correct answer is Vinegar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tomato**:

 
 
• Tomatoes are a natural source of **Oxalic acid** and **Malic acid**.
 
• They also contain small amounts of **Citric acid**. Oxalic acid is a **dicarboxylic acid** that occurs naturally in many vegetables and fruits.
 
 
 
• **Orange**:
 
 
• Oranges, along with other **citrus fruits** like lemons and limes, are the primary sources of **Citric acid**.
 
• They are also rich in **Ascorbic acid**, which is commonly known as **Vitamin C**. Citric acid is responsible for the tart flavor of citrus fruits.
 
 
 
• **Tamarind**:
 
 
• Tamarind is a rich source of **Tartaric acid**.
 
• **Tartaric acid** is a white, crystalline organic acid that occurs naturally in many fruits, most notably in **grapes** and **tamarinds**. It is often used as an **antioxidant** in food products.
 
 
 
• **Other Natural Acids**:
 
 
• **Lactic Acid**: Found in **sour milk** and **curd** due to the action of Lactobacillus bacteria on lactose.
 
• **Methanoic Acid (Formic Acid)**: Found in **ant stings** and **nettle stings**, causing a burning sensation upon injection into the skin.
 
• **Malic Acid**: Predominantly found in **apples** and pears, contributing to their sour taste when unripe.
 
• **Amino Acids**: These are the **building blocks of proteins** found in meat, beans, and legumes.

questions.question: In human beings, excretory products in the form of soluble nitrogen compounds are removed by the ______ in the kidneys.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nephrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nephrons** are the **microscopic structural and functional units** of the **kidneys**. Each human kidney contains approximately **1 million** to **1.2 million** nephrons.
 
• The primary role of the **nephron** is to process **blood** to remove **metabolic waste** and perform **osmoregulation**.
 
• It filters out **soluble nitrogenous compounds**, primarily **urea**, along with excess **salts** and **water** from the bloodstream to form **urine**.
 
• The filtration process begins in the **Glomerulus**, a high-pressure capillary bed, where **fluid** is pushed into the **Bowman's capsule**.
 
• As the filtrate moves through the **renal tubule**, essential substances like **glucose**, **amino acids**, and **electrolytes** are selectively reabsorbed back into the **blood**.
 
• The remaining concentrated fluid, containing **waste products**, is then collected as **urine** and moved toward the **renal pelvis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urethra:**

 
 
• The **urethra** is a muscular tube that conveys **urine** from the **urinary bladder** to the outside of the body.
 
• Unlike the **nephron**, it does not perform **filtration** or **waste removal** from the blood; it strictly serves as an **excretory passage**.
 
 
 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate):**
 
 
• **ATP** is known as the **energy currency** of the cell. It is a **nucleotide** that stores and transfers **chemical energy** within cells for metabolism.
 
• While **ATP** provides the energy required for **active transport** in the **kidney tubules**, it is not a physical structure involved in filtering **nitrogenous waste**.
 
 
 
• **Xylem:**
 
 
• **Xylem** is a specialized **vascular tissue** found in **plants**, not in humans.
 
• Its primary function is the **conduction of water** and **dissolved minerals** from the **roots** to the rest of the plant.
 
• It also provides **mechanical support** to the plant structure through **lignified** cell walls.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogenous Wastes in Humans:**
 
 
• Humans are **ureotelic** organisms, meaning we primarily excrete **nitrogen** in the form of **urea**.
 
• **Urea** is produced in the **liver** through the **ornithine cycle** (urea cycle) as a less toxic alternative to **ammonia**.
 
• Efficient removal of these **solutes** is vital to prevent **uremia**, a dangerous accumulation of **waste** in the **blood**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kidney Function:** Apart from **excretion**, kidneys regulate **blood pressure** via the **Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS)** and stimulate **red blood cell** production by secreting **erythropoietin**.
 
• **Homeostasis:** The **nephrons** maintain the **acid-base balance** (pH) of the body by secreting **hydrogen ions** and reabsorbing **bicarbonate ions**.
 
• **Ureter vs. Urethra:** It is important to distinguish between the two; **ureters** carry urine from the **kidneys** to the **bladder**, while the **urethra** carries it from the **bladder** to the external environment.

questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya defeated the Greek satraps left behind by Alexander in the ______ and integrated the region into an empire that stretched from the northern plains to the Deccan plateau.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**northwest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya**, the founder of the **Mauryan Empire**, led a campaign to liberate the **northwest** region of the Indian subcontinent from the remnants of Greek rule following the death of **Alexander the Great** in **323 BCE**.
 
• After Alexander's departure, the territories in the **Indus Valley** and **Punjab** were governed by **Greek satraps**. Chandragupta mobilized an army, overthrew these governors, and established his authority over the **northwestern** frontiers.
 
• The most significant conflict in this region occurred in **305 BCE**, when **Seleucus I Nicator**, a general of Alexander and the founder of the **Seleucid Empire**, crossed the **Indus River** to reclaim Alexander's lost territories.
 
• Chandragupta defeated **Seleucus Nicator**, leading to a historic peace treaty. Under this agreement, the **northwest** provinces of **Arachosia** (Kandahar), **Gedrosia** (Balochistan), and **Paropamisadae** (Kabul) were ceded to the Mauryan Empire.
 
• By securing the **northwest**, Chandragupta integrated a vast territory that stretched from the **Indus** to the **Hindu Kush** mountains, eventually expanding his empire across the **northern plains** down to the **Deccan plateau**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Foundation of the Empire:** Chandragupta Maurya established the empire in **322 BCE** after defeating **Dhana Nanda**, the last ruler of the **Nanda Dynasty**, with the strategic guidance of his mentor, **Chanakya** (also known as **Kautilya**).
 
• **Chanakya and Statecraft:** **Chanakya** authored the **Arthashastra**, a seminal work on **political science**, **economics**, and **military strategy**, which served as the administrative backbone for the Mauryan state.
 
• **Diplomatic Relations:** Following the treaty with **Seleucus**, a diplomatic relationship was established between the Greeks and Indians. **Megasthenes** was sent as a Greek ambassador to the Mauryan capital of **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna).
 
• **Indica by Megasthenes:** The book **Indica**, written by **Megasthenes**, provides detailed accounts of the **Mauryan administration**, social classes, and the grandeur of the capital city.
 
• **Territorial Extent:** At its peak under Chandragupta, the empire was one of the largest in the world, covering almost the entire Indian subcontinent except for the extreme south and **Kalinga** (which was later conquered by his grandson, **Ashoka**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **War Elephants:** As part of the peace treaty in **305 BCE**, Chandragupta gifted **500 war elephants** to **Seleucus**. These elephants were later instrumental in Seleucus's victory at the **Battle of Ipsus** in **301 BCE**.
 
• **Religious Transition:** According to **Jain traditions**, toward the end of his life, Chandragupta Maurya abdicated his throne, embraced **Jainism** under the monk **Bhadrabahu**, and migrated to **Shravanabelagola** in present-day **Karnataka**.
 
• **Administrative Units:** The empire was divided into four main provinces, with the **northwest** province having its headquarters at **Takshashila** (Taxila), which was a major center for **learning** and **commerce**.
 
• **Unification of India:** Chandragupta is often credited as the first ruler to achieve the **political unification** of India, bringing diverse regions under a single **centralized administration**.

questions.question: The 'Lion and Peacock' dance is a folk dance of which Indian state/Union Territory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Lion and Peacock dance** is a traditional folk dance originating from the state of **Arunachal Pradesh** in Northeast India.
 
• It is a specialized **mask dance** performed primarily by the **Monpa tribe**, who reside in the **Tawang** and **West Kameng** districts of the state.
 
• This dance form is characterized by performers wearing **elaborate masks** and costumes that mimic the movements, grace, and characteristics of a **lion** and a **peacock**.
 
• The dance is a significant part of the cultural festivities during **Losar**, which is the **Tibetan New Year** celebrated by the Buddhist communities in the region.
 
• It symbolizes the **harmonious relationship**

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is known as the '100-drum festival' and is celebrated by the Garo tribes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wangala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Wangala Festival** is the most significant cultural event for the **Garo tribe**, primarily inhabiting the **Garo Hills** in **Meghalaya**, as well as parts of **Assam** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• It is widely recognized as the **"100-Drum Festival"** because of the traditional ritual where **100 drums** (long oval-shaped drums known as **Nagras**) are beaten in a rhythmic symphony by men.
 
• This festival is a **post-harvest thanksgiving** ceremony held to honor **Saljong**, the **Sun God** and the deity of fertility, for a bountiful harvest and to seek blessings for the upcoming agricultural cycle.
 
• The celebration typically takes place in the month of **November** every year, marking the end of the period of toil in the fields.
 
• The main event is characterized by the **Wangala Dance**, where men and women dressed in colorful traditional attire with feathered headgear dance to the tunes of drums, flutes, and brass instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hornbill Festival:**

 
 
• Known as the **"Festival of Festivals,"** it is celebrated in **Nagaland** from **December 1st to 10th** annually.
 
• It aims to protect and revive the rich culture of the **Naga tribes** and is held at the **Kisama Heritage Village** near **Kohima**.
 
• The festival features traditional Naga dances, folk songs, indigenous games, and the famous **Hornbill International Rock Contest**.
 
 
 
• **Chhekar Festival:**
 
 
• This is a religious festival of the **Monpa tribe**, who reside in the **Tawang** and **West Kameng** districts of **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• It is performed to protect the village and crops from **evil spirits** and natural disasters, involving the chanting of Buddhist scriptures.
 
• The festival reflects the deep influence of **Tibetan Buddhism** on the Monpa culture.
 
 
 
• **Laru Kaj:**
 
 
• This is a traditional festival of the **Gond tribe**, particularly found in **Madhya Pradesh** and **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **Narayan Deo** and involves rituals for the health and prosperity of the family and their **livestock**, specifically involving the sacrifice of a pig in some traditions.
 
• It is an intimate family festival rather than a large community-wide public gathering.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Garo Society:** The Garos are one of the few remaining **matrilineal** societies in the world, where the youngest daughter (**Nokna**) inherits the family property and children take their mother's clan name.
 
• **Venue:** While celebrated in various villages, the state-level **Hundred Drums Wangala Festival** is grandly organized at **Asanang**, near **Tura** in the West Garo Hills district of **Meghalaya**.
 
• **Significance of Instruments:** Apart from the **Nagras**, instruments like the **Adil** (a trumpet made of buffalo horn) and **Singga** are integral to the musical landscape of the **Wangala** festival.
 
• **Rituals:** The festival begins with a ceremony called **Rugala**, where the first-hand liquor of the harvest is offered to the deity, followed by **Chaachat Soa** (incense burning).

questions.question: Which of the following rulers forced to give over half of his territory to the East India Company in 1801?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nawab of Awadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1801**, the **Nawab of Awadh** was forced to cede over half of his territory to the **British East India Company** because he failed to pay for the "subsidiary forces" maintained by the British.
 
• The Governor-General of India at that time was **Lord Wellesley** (who served from **1798 to 1805**). He used the **Subsidiary Alliance** system as a tool for political expansion and to establish British paramountcy over Indian princely states.
 
• The specific territories surrendered by the **Nawab Saadat Ali Khan II** included **Rohilkhand** and the **Lower Doab**. This was done under the pressure of the **Subsidiary Alliance** treaty. ***Hence, the Nawab of Awadh is the correct answer.***
 
• Under this arrangement, the **Nawab** was required to disband his own military forces and accept a **British Resident** at his court, effectively losing control over foreign affairs and defense.
 
• The reduction of **Awadh's** territory allowed the British to surround the state almost entirely, turning it into a "buffer state" between the Company's territories and the **Maratha Empire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Subsidiary Alliance System:**

 
 
• It was a "non-intervention" policy used by the **British East India Company** to establish its **hegemony**. The ruler of an allying Indian state was compelled to accept the permanent stationing of a **British force** within his territory and to pay a subsidy for its maintenance.
 
• The first state to accept the **Subsidiary Alliance** was the **Nizam of Hyderabad** in **1798**. Other states like **Mysore (1799)** and the **Peshwa (1802)** soon followed.
 
 
 
• **Nawab of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa:**
 
 
• The **Nawabs of Bengal**, who also controlled **Bihar** and **Orissa**, had already lost significant power much earlier. Following the **Battle of Buxar (1764)** and the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**, the **Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II** granted the **Diwani rights** (right to collect revenue) of **Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa** to the Company.
 
• By **1801**, these regions were already directly administered or heavily controlled by the British through the **Dual System of Government** or direct rule, unlike the territorial ceding specifically demanded from **Awadh** in that year.
 
 
 
• **Annexation of Awadh (1856):**
 
 
• The final blow to the **Awadh** dynasty came in **1856**. Despite the **Subsidiary Alliance**, **Lord Dalhousie** annexed **Awadh** on the grounds of **"maladministration"** or misgovernance.
 
• The last **Nawab**, **Wajid Ali Shah**, was dethroned and exiled to **Calcutta**. This annexation was a major grievance that led to the **Revolt of 1857**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Consequences for the Rulers:**

 
 
• Rulers who entered the **Subsidiary Alliance** could not employ any **European** (other than British) in their service without prior approval. They also could not negotiate with any other Indian ruler without consulting the **Governor-General**.
 
• While it offered "protection" from external enemies, it led to the total **disarmament** of the local princely states and their eventual economic collapse due to the heavy subsidies demanded by the **British**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Awadh:**
 
 
• The **1801 Treaty** saw the **British** taking over the most fertile parts of **Awadh**. This increased the revenue for the Company and strengthened their strategic position in **North India**.
 
• By reducing the **Nawab** to a mere figurehead, the **British** ensured that **Awadh** would remain subservient until its total absorption into the **British Empire** five decades later.

questions.question: The motion of the moon around the earth is due to the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**centripetal force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The motion of the **Moon** around the **Earth** is a form of **circular motion** (specifically, an elliptical orbit that is nearly circular). For any object to maintain a circular path, it requires a force acting towards the center of the circle.
 
• This "center-seeking" force is known as **centripetal force**. It is not a new kind of force but a role played by an existing force in the system. ***Hence, the correct answer is centripetal force.***
 
• In the **Earth-Moon system**, the necessary **centripetal force** is provided by the **gravitational force** of attraction between the **Earth** and the **Moon**.
 
• If this **centripetal force** were absent, the **Moon** would cease its orbital motion and fly off in a straight line along the **tangent** to the circular path due to **inertia**.
 
• The **centripetal force** causes a continuous change in the **direction** of the **Moon's velocity** at every point in its orbit, which means the **Moon** is constantly **accelerating** towards the **Earth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation**: Formulated in **1687** by **Sir Isaac Newton**, it states that every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• **Magnetic Field**: This refers to the region around a magnetic material or a moving electric charge within which the force of magnetism acts. While the **Earth** has a strong **magnetic field** (the **magnetosphere**), it does not govern the orbital motion of celestial bodies like the **Moon**.
 
• **Friction Force**: This is a force that resists the relative motion of solid surfaces, fluid layers, and material elements sliding against each other. Since space is a **vacuum**, there is no air or surface to provide **friction** to the **Moon**; if friction were present, the **Moon** would eventually lose energy and crash into the **Earth**.
 
• **Acceleration**: While the **Moon** does experience **centripetal acceleration**, acceleration is the **effect** of the force, not the **cause** of the motion. The question asks for the force "due to" which the motion occurs.
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion**: When an object moves in a circle at a **constant speed**, its **velocity** is constantly changing because its direction is changing. This change in velocity over time is what defines **acceleration** in an orbit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Orbital Speed**: The **Moon** travels at an average speed of approximately **1.022 kilometers per second** (about **3,679 km/h**) to maintain its balance between **gravity** and **inertia**.
 
• **Distance**: The average distance from the **Earth** to the **Moon** is approximately **384,400 kilometers**. This distance is critical in calculating the magnitude of the **gravitational force**.
 
• **Revolution Period**: It takes the **Moon** about **27.3 days** to complete one **sidereal revolution** around the **Earth**.
 
• **Satellite Motion**: The same principles of **centripetal force** and **gravity** apply to **artificial satellites** launched by organizations like **ISRO** or **NASA**. To stay in orbit, they must reach a specific **orbital velocity**.
 
• **Tidal Effects**: The **gravitational pull** of the **Moon** on the **Earth's** oceans is the primary cause of **tides**, demonstrating that the force is mutual as per **Newton's Third Law of Motion**.

questions.question: As of August 2025, Jupiter has ______ moons that are officially recognized by the International Astronomical Union.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**95**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **August 2025**, **Jupiter** has **95 moons** that are officially recognized and tracked by the **International Astronomical Union (IAU)** and its **Minor Planet Center (MPC)**.
 
• The most significant recent update to this count occurred in early **2023**, when **12 new moons** were officially added to the tally following observations by a team led by astronomer **Scott Sheppard** of the **Carnegie Institution for Science**.
 
• These observations were conducted using the **Magellan telescope** in **Chile** and the **Subaru telescope** in **Hawaii** between **2021** and **2022**, with the orbital data confirmed in **February 2023**.
 
• Most of the newly recognized moons are quite small, measuring between **1 and 3 kilometers** in diameter, and they reside in **outer orbits** that are **retrograde** (moving in the opposite direction of Jupiter's rotation).
 
• Of the **95 moons**, **72** are classified as **irregular moons** with distant, eccentric orbits, while the remaining moons belong to the inner regular groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Galilean Moons**:

 
 
• These are the four largest moons of Jupiter: **Io**, **Europa**, **Ganymede**, and **Callisto**.
 
• They were discovered by **Galileo Galilei** in **January 1610** using a homemade telescope, providing the first evidence of celestial bodies orbiting a planet other than Earth.
 
• **Ganymede** is the **largest moon** in the **Solar System**, even larger than the planet **Mercury**, and is the only moon known to possess its own **magnetic field**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Saturn**:
 
 
• For a brief period in **2023**, Jupiter was considered the planet with the most moons; however, **Saturn** reclaimed the title later that year.
 
• As of **2024-2025**, **Saturn** remains the leader with **146 moons** officially recognized by the **IAU**.
 
 
 
• **Space Exploration Missions**:
 
 
• The **JUICE (JUpiter ICy moons Explorer)** mission by the **European Space Agency (ESA)** was launched in **April 2023** to study **Ganymede**, **Callisto**, and **Europa**.
 
• **NASA’s Europa Clipper** mission, launched in **October 2024**, is scheduled to arrive at Jupiter in **2030** to investigate the habitability of **Europa** and its subsurface ocean.
 
• NASA's **Juno spacecraft** has been in orbit around Jupiter since **July 2016**, providing high-resolution data on the planet's atmosphere and its larger satellites.
 
 
 
• **Categorization of Moons**:
 
 
• **Regular Satellites**: These include the **Inner Moons** (Metis, Adrastea, Amalthea, and Thebe) and the **Galilean Moons**, which have nearly circular orbits.
 
• **Irregular Satellites**: These are typically smaller bodies captured by Jupiter's gravity; they are often grouped into families such as the **Himalia group** (prograde) and the **Carme, Ananke, and Pasiphae groups** (retrograde).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Naming Conventions**: The **International Astronomical Union** oversees the official naming of moons. While many of Jupiter's moons have names from **Greek** and **Roman mythology** (specifically lovers or descendants of **Zeus/Jupiter**), many of the **95 moons** are still designated by **alphanumeric codes** (e.g., S/2003 J 24) until their orbits are precisely determined.
 
• **Jupiter's Mass**: Jupiter is the **largest planet** in the solar system, with a mass **318 times** that of **Earth**. Its massive **gravitational field** allows it to maintain such a large and diverse system of satellites.
 
• **Great Red Spot**: Apart from its moons, Jupiter is famous for its **Great Red Spot**, a giant storm that has been raging for at least **350 years** and is larger than the diameter of Earth.

questions.question:
Which of the following factor affect the distribution of population?

I. Soil

II. Minerals
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soil** is a crucial geographical factor that determines the distribution of the population. Fertile soils are essential for **agricultural activities**, which support large populations by ensuring **food security**.
 
• Areas with **fertile alluvial soils**, such as the **Ganga and Brahmaputra plains** in **India**, the **Hwang-He** and **Chang Jiang** in **China**, and the **Nile** valley in **Egypt**, are among the most **densely populated** regions in the world. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Minerals** significantly influence population distribution by attracting industries and creating **employment opportunities**. Regions with rich **mineral deposits** often become hubs for mining and manufacturing activities.
 
• For instance, the discovery of **diamonds** in **South Africa** and **oil** in the **Middle East** led to the settlement of people in these previously sparsely populated areas. Similarly, the **Chhota Nagpur Plateau** in **India** is a major population center due to its vast **mineral wealth**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

• **Pattern of Distribution:** The way in which people are spread across the earth's surface is known as the **pattern of population distribution**. More than **90%** of the world's population lives in about **30%** of the land surface.

questions.question:
Which of the following is correct regarding sound waves?

I. Compression – Region of high pressure

II. Rarefaction – Region of low pressure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sound waves** are **longitudinal waves** that propagate through a medium via a series of **compressions** and **rarefactions**.
 
• A **Compression** is a region in a **longitudinal wave** where the particles of the medium are closest together. This results in a region of **high pressure** and **high density** because the volume of the medium decreases locally. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• A **Rarefaction** is a region in a **longitudinal wave** where the particles of the medium are spread furthest apart. This creates a region of **low pressure** and **low density**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• These regions of pressure variations travel through the medium, allowing **energy** to be transferred from one point to another without the permanent displacement of the particles themselves.
 
• The distance between two consecutive **compressions** or two consecutive **rarefactions** is defined as the **wavelength** of the sound wave.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both I and II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Sound Waves:**

 
 
• Sound is a **mechanical wave**, meaning it requires a **material medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) for its propagation. It cannot travel through a **vacuum** as there are no particles to compress or rarefy.
 
• In **longitudinal waves**, the individual particles of the medium move in a direction **parallel** to the direction of propagation of the wave disturbance.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Sound:**
 
 
• **Frequency:** Measured in **Hertz (Hz)**, it determines the **pitch** of the sound. Humans can generally hear sounds in the range of **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
• **Amplitude:** It determines the **loudness** or intensity of the sound. A larger amplitude means a louder sound.
 
• **Speed of Sound:** The **speed** depends on the **elasticity** and **density** of the medium. Sound travels fastest in **solids** (e.g., **Steel**), followed by **liquids** (e.g., **Water**), and slowest in **gases** (e.g., **Air**).
 
• In **Air** at **0°C**, the speed of sound is approximately **331 m/s**, and at **20°C**, it is about **343 m/s**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pressure and Density Relationship:**

 
 
• In the context of sound waves, **pressure** and **density** are directly proportional. A region of **high density** (compression) is always a region of **high pressure**, and a region of **low density** (rarefaction) is always a region of **low pressure**.
 
 
 
• **Wave Propagation:**
 
 
• The **vibration** of an object (like a tuning fork or vocal cords) creates the initial **disturbance**. As the source moves **forward**, it pushes the air particles, creating **compression**. As it moves **backward**, it creates a space for particles to spread, resulting in **rarefaction**.
 
• **Echo** is the reflection of these sound waves when they hit a hard surface. To hear a distinct echo, the minimum distance between the source and the obstacle should be approximately **17.2 meters** in air.

questions.question: In India, Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) project was conceived in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC)** project was formally conceived in **April 2005**. The initiative was part of a strategic discussion during the **India-Japan Summit**, where both nations agreed to cooperate on rail sector development.
 
• Following the announcement in **2005**, the **Ministry of Railways** initiated the planning process to address the saturation of the existing **Golden Quadrilateral** rail routes, which were struggling to handle the rising demand for freight and passenger traffic.
 
• To implement this ambitious project, the **Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL)** was incorporated on **30th October 2006**. It was established as a **Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)** under the **Ministry of Railways** to undertake planning, development, and mobilization of financial resources.
 
• The primary objective of the **DFC** project is to create a high-speed, high-capacity railway network specifically for goods trains, thereby reducing the transit time and **logistics costs** in **India**.
 
• The project was initially approved as part of the **11th Five Year Plan** of the **Government of India**, focusing on the construction of the **Eastern** and **Western** corridors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC):**

 
 
• The **WDFC** covers a distance of approximately **1,504 km**. It connects **Dadri** in **Uttar Pradesh** to **Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT)** in **Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• This corridor is largely funded by the **Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)** through a soft loan. It passes through states including **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and **Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC):**
 
 
• The **EDFC** spans about **1,875 km**, starting from **Sahnewal (Ludhiana)** in **Punjab** and terminating at **Dankuni** in **West Bengal**.
 
• The **World Bank** has provided significant financial assistance for the construction of specific segments of the **EDFC**, which is vital for transporting **coal** and **steel** from Eastern India.
 
 
 
• **Technical Features:**
 
 
• The corridors are designed for **heavy axle loads** of **25 to 32.5 tonnes**, compared to the standard **22.5 tonnes** on existing Indian tracks.
 
• Trains on these tracks are expected to reach a **maximum speed** of **100 km/h**, significantly improving the efficiency of the **Indian Railways** freight operations.
 
 
 
• **Future Expansion (GQFC):**
 
 
• Beyond the initial two corridors, the **Government of India** plans to develop the **Golden Quadrilateral Freight Corridor (GQFC)**, which includes the **North-South (Delhi-Chennai)**, **East-West (Kolkata-Mumbai)**, and **East Coast** corridors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **DFC** project is crucial for the **Make in India** initiative as it enhances **multimodal transport** efficiency and supports **Industrial Corridors** like the **Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC)**.
 
• By separating freight from passenger traffic, the **Indian Railways** can improve the **punctuality** of passenger trains and increase the **throughput** of goods, contributing to **GDP growth**.
 
• The **Dedicated Freight Corridors** utilize **long-haul trains** (up to **1.5 km** long) and **double-stack container** technology (primarily on the **WDFC**) to maximize cargo volume per trip.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of Judo Belt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rainbow Belt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rainbow Belt** is not a recognized or official rank in the **Judo** grading system. While some children's programs in other martial arts might use "multi-color" belts for motivation, the **International Judo Federation (IJF)** and the **Kodokan** do not recognize it. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **Brown Belt** is a legitimate and significant rank in **Judo**. It represents the highest levels of the **Kyu** (student) grades, typically encompassing **1st Kyu**, **2nd Kyu**, and **3rd Kyu**, depending on the national federation's specific guidelines. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Red and White Belt**, also known as the **Kohaku obi**, is an official belt used to designate high-ranking masters. It is specifically worn by practitioners who have attained the ranks of **6th**, **7th**, and **8th Dan**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Black colour Belt** (or **Kuro obi**) is perhaps the most famous martial arts belt, signifying that a practitioner has graduated from the **Kyu** levels to the **Dan** (expert) levels. It begins at **1st Dan** (Shodan). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The grading system in **Judo** was developed to provide a visible structure for a student's progress in **technique**, **philosophy**, and **competitive prowess**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origins of the Belt System:**

 
 
• **Judo** was founded by **Kano Jigoro** in **1882** in **Japan**. He is credited with creating the modern **Dan/Kyu** ranking system and using colored belts to distinguish between different levels of expertise.
 
• Initially, only **white** and **black** belts were used. The expanded color palette (yellow, orange, green, blue, brown) was introduced later, particularly as **Judo** spread to **Europe** and the **Americas** in the **mid-20th century**.
 
 
 
• **Kyu (Student) Ranks:**
 
 
• Beginners in **Judo** start with a **White Belt** (6th Kyu).
 
• As they progress, they move through colors such as **Yellow**, **Orange**, **Green**, **Blue**, and finally **Brown**.
 
• The specific order and number of **Kyu** grades can vary slightly by **country**; for example, the **United States**, **United Kingdom**, and **Japan** have minor differences in their color sequences.
 
 
 
• **Dan (Master) Ranks:**
 
 
• **1st Dan to 5th Dan** practitioners wear a solid **Black Belt**.
 
• **6th Dan to 8th Dan** masters have the option to wear the **Red and White** paneled belt.
 
• **9th Dan and 10th Dan**, the highest attainable ranks, are entitled to wear a solid **Red Belt**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Kodokan:** Located in **Tokyo**, it is the headquarters of the worldwide **Judo** community. The **Kodokan** maintains the strictest standards for **Dan** promotions and historical accuracy of the sport.
 
• **Criteria for Promotion:** Advancing through the belts requires more than just time. Students must demonstrate proficiency in **Nage-waza** (throwing techniques), **Katame-waza** (grappling techniques), and **Kata** (formalized patterns).
 
• **Minimum Age:** Many federations have a **minimum age** requirement for the **Black Belt**, often **15 or 16 years old**, ensuring that the practitioner has the physical and mental maturity required for the rank.
 
• **Competitive Points:** In many systems, a "batsugun" promotion can occur if a **judoka** defeats a certain number of higher-ranked opponents in **sanctioned tournaments**.

questions.question: The Chelliah Committee recommended in January ____ that the prevailing rates of import duties be rationalised and lowered.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1993**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tax Reforms Committee** was set up by the **Government of India** in **August 1991** under the chairmanship of **Dr. Raja J. Chelliah** to examine the existing tax structure and provide a roadmap for reform.
 
• The committee submitted its final report in **January 1993**, which contained comprehensive recommendations for rationalizing both **direct and indirect taxes**.
 
• A major focus of the **January 1993** report was the rationalization and lowering of **import duties** (customs duties), which were among the highest in the world at that time. ***Hence, the year mentioned in the question is correct as 1993.***
 
• The committee recommended reducing the **peak customs duty** from the then-prevailing levels of over **150%** to about **50%** by the year **1995-96**.
 
• It also proposed a simplified **multi-tier tax structure** to reduce administrative complexity and minimize tax evasion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Broad Recommendations of the Chelliah Committee:**

 
 
• **Direct Taxes:** The committee suggested reducing the **personal income tax** rates to a maximum of **40%** and the **corporate tax** rate to **40%** for domestic companies to encourage compliance.
 
• **Indirect Taxes:** Apart from customs duties, it recommended the introduction of a **Value Added Tax (VAT)** system to replace the existing cascading **excise duty** structure.
 
• **Tax Base Expansion:** It emphasized **broadening the tax base** by bringing more services and people under the tax net while reducing the number of **exemptions** and deductions.
 
 
 
• **Context of 1991 Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• The **Chelliah Committee** was a vital part of the **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms initiated under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• Before **1991**, India followed a high-tariff regime with **import duties** reaching as high as **300%** in some cases, which hindered **international trade** and industrial efficiency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy of Raja J. Chelliah:**

 
 
• **Dr. Raja J. Chelliah** is often referred to as the **"Father of Tax Reforms"** in India due to his pioneering work in shifting the Indian economy towards a modern, transparent tax system.
 
• His recommendations led to the gradual reduction of **import duties** in subsequent Union Budgets, making Indian industry more competitive globally.
 
 
 
• **Timeline of Reports:**
 
 
• **Interim Report:** Submitted in **December 1991**, focusing on immediate changes needed in the **1992-93 Budget**.
 
• **Final Report (Part I):** Submitted in **August 1992**.
 
• **Final Report (Part II):** Submitted in **January 1993**, which detailed the long-term vision for **customs duty rationalization** and tax administration.

questions.question: Lad Khan Temple is located in which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lad Khan Temple** is located in **Aihole**, which is situated in the **Bagalkot district** of the state of **Karnataka**, India.
 
• Constructed in the **5th century AD**, it is considered one of the oldest structures in the region and was built during the reign of the **Early Chalukya dynasty**.
 
• The temple is primarily dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and houses a **Shiva Linga** in its inner sanctum, although historical evidence suggests it might have been originally dedicated to **Surya** (the Sun God).
 
• The unusual name "**Lad Khan**" is not reflective of its religious origin; it is named after a **Muslim prince** who lived in the temple for a period during the **19th century**.
 
• The temple architecture is noted for its **square plan** and a **flat roof** made of massive **stone slabs**, representing a crucial phase in the evolution of **Hindu temple architecture** from cave shelters to free-standing structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aihole: The Cradle of Indian Architecture:**

 
 
• **Aihole** is often described as the "**Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture**" because it served as a site where **Chalukyan architects** experimented with various styles and designs.
 
• The **Aihole complex** contains over **120 stone temples** dating from the **4th to the 12th century**, including the famous **Durga Temple** and the **Ravana Phadi Cave**.
 
 
 
• **Chalukyan Dynasty and Art:**
 
 
• The **Chalukyas of Badami** were great patrons of art and architecture, establishing their power in the **Deccan** region during the **6th century**.
 
• The architectural style developed by them is known as the **Vesara style**, which blends elements of the **Nagara** (North Indian) and **Dravida** (South Indian) styles of temple building.
 
• Their major centers of construction included **Badami**, **Aihole**, and **Pattadakal**.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features of Lad Khan Temple:**
 
 
• The temple features a **Mukhamandapa** (pillared porch) and a **Sabhamandapa** (great hall) leading to the **Garbhagriha** (sanctum).
 
• The **pillars** are decorated with intricate carvings, and the exterior walls feature **lattice windows** (Jalis) that allow light to enter the interior, a characteristic feature of **early Chalukyan** work.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical and Historical Context:**

 
 
• The temples at **Aihole**, **Badami**, and **Pattadakal** are located along the **Malaprabha River** valley in **Karnataka**.
 
• While **Aihole** was the early administrative center, **Pattadakal** eventually became the site for **royal coronations** and is now a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
 
 
• **Material and Construction:**
 
 
• The **Lad Khan Temple** was constructed using **sandstone** that was joined without mortar, using the **dry masonry** technique typical of the era.
 
• The **Nandi** (the sacred bull) is placed in the center of the hall, facing the **Shiva Linga**, which is a standard iconographic arrangement in **Shaivite temples**.
 
• The temple represents the **Panchayatana** style of architecture, though it is one of the more primitive versions of this layout.

questions.question: The Sanchi Stupa gateways are known for sculptures depicting scenes from ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jataka stories**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The gateways of the **Great Stupa at Sanchi**, also known as **Toranas**, are world-renowned for their detailed and intricate **sculptural narratives**.
 
• These sculptures primarily depict various **Jataka stories**, which are a voluminous body of literature native to **India** concerning the previous births of **Gautama Buddha** in both human and animal form.
 
• Apart from the **Jataka tales**, the gateways also illustrate important **historical events** from the life of the **Buddha**, such as his **birth**, the **Great Departure** (leaving his palace), his **Enlightenment**, and his **first sermon** at Sarnath.
 
• A unique feature of these carvings is the **aniconic representation** of the **Buddha**; he is never shown in human form but is represented through symbols like the **Bodhi tree**, a **wheel** (Dharmachakra), an **empty throne**, or **footprints**.
 
• While the original brick stupa was built by **Emperor Ashoka**, the ornate **stone gateways** and the railing were added later, mostly during the **1st century BCE** under the **Satavahana Dynasty**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Location and Heritage:** The **Sanchi Stupa** is located in the **Raisen district** of **Madhya Pradesh**, India. It was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1989** due to its significance as the oldest stone structure in India.
 
• **Specific Jataka Depictions:** Several famous stories are carved on the pillars and architraves, including the **Vessantara Jataka** (highlighting the virtue of charity), the **Chhaddanta Jataka** (story of the six-tusked elephant), and the **Mahakapi Jataka** (where the **Buddha** was a monkey king).
 
• **The Four Gateways:**
 
 
• **South Gateway:** The oldest of the four, featuring the **birth of Buddha** and Ashoka's visit to the **Ramagrama Stupa**.
 
• **North Gateway:** Crowned by a **Wheel of Law**, it depicts many miracles performed by the **Buddha**.
 
• **East Gateway:** Illustrates the **Great Departure** of Prince **Siddhartha** from **Kapilavastu**.
 
• **West Gateway:** Known for depicting the **Seven incarnations** of the **Buddha** and the **war over the relics**.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options Analysis:**
 
 
• **Vedas:** These are the oldest scriptures of **Hinduism**. While historically significant, they are not the subject of the Buddhist art at **Sanchi**.
 
• **Ramayana:** An ancient Indian epic. While scenes from the **Ramayana** appear in later **Hindu temple** architecture, they are not found on the **Sanchi** gateways.
 
• **Mahavir Jain's life:** **Lord Mahavira** was the 24th Tirthankara of **Jainism**. His life stories are depicted in Jain sites like **Dilwara** or **Palitana**, but not at the Buddhist site of **Sanchi**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architectural Components:** The **Sanchi Stupa** consists of a hemispherical dome called the **Anda**, a square railing at the top called the **Harmika**, and a central pillar supporting three umbrellas known as the **Chatra**.
 
• **Discovery and Restoration:** The site was "discovered" by **General Taylor** in **1818**. Later, **Sir John Marshall**, the Director-General of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, played a pivotal role in its restoration between **1912 and 1919**.
 
• **Flora and Fauna:** The carvings are also noted for their realistic portrayal of **animals** (elephants, lions, bulls) and **nature motifs**, showcasing the deep connection between early **Buddhism** and the natural world.
 
• **Inscriptions:** There are over **600 inscriptions** on the stones of **Sanchi**, many of which record donations made by ordinary people, including **merchants**, **monks**, and **nuns**, indicating that it was a site of mass devotion.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a postulate of Dalton's atomic theory?

I. All matter is made of very tiny particles called atoms, which participate in chemical reactions.

II. Atoms are indivisible particles, which cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dalton's Atomic Theory**, proposed by the British chemist **John Dalton** in **1808**, provided a scientific explanation for the laws of chemical combination.
 
• According to the theory, **all matter**, whether an element, a compound, or a mixture, is composed of very small particles called **atoms**. These atoms are the basic units that take part in **chemical reactions**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• One of the most fundamental postulates of this theory is that **atoms are indivisible particles**. This means they cannot be subdivided into smaller parts (though modern science later discovered subatomic particles).
 
• The theory also states that atoms **cannot be created or destroyed** in a chemical reaction, which provides a theoretical basis for the **Law of Conservation of Mass**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• ***Therefore, both statements I and II are valid postulates of Dalton's atomic theory.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Postulates regarding Elements:**

 
 
• Dalton stated that **atoms of a given element** are **identical in mass** and **chemical properties**. This means every atom of **Hydrogen** is exactly like every other atom of **Hydrogen** in terms of its weight and how it reacts.
 
• Conversely, **atoms of different elements** possess **different masses** and **different chemical properties**. For example, an atom of **Oxygen** has a different mass and set of characteristics compared to an atom of **Carbon**.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Compounds:**
 
 
• The theory explains that **atoms combine** in the ratio of **small whole numbers** to form **compounds**. This explains the **Law of Constant Proportions** (or Definite Proportions).
 
• In any given compound, the **relative number** and **kinds of atoms** are **constant**. For example, in a water molecule (**H2O**), there are always **2 atoms** of **Hydrogen** for every **1 atom** of **Oxygen**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• John Dalton published his ideas in a book titled **"A New System of Chemical Philosophy"**.
 
• Before Dalton, the idea of atoms was purely philosophical; his work turned it into a **quantitative scientific model** that could be tested through experimentation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Limitations of Dalton's Theory:**

 
 
• While revolutionary, the theory had limitations. The discovery of **subatomic particles** like **electrons**, **protons**, and **neutrons** later proved that atoms are, in fact, **divisible**.
 
• The discovery of **isotopes** (atoms of the same element with different masses, such as **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-14**) challenged the postulate that all atoms of a given element have identical masses.
 
• The discovery of **isobars** (atoms of different elements having the same atomic mass, such as **Argon** and **Calcium** both having a mass of **40**) challenged the idea that different elements must have different masses.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle was discovered by J. Chadwick in 1932?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neutron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Neutron** was discovered by the British physicist **James Chadwick** in **1932**. He performed an experiment where he bombarded **Beryllium** with **alpha particles**, which resulted in the emission of a new type of radiation consisting of uncharged particles.
 
• A **neutron** is a subatomic particle that has **no net electric charge** (it is neutral) and a mass slightly larger than that of a **proton**. ***Hence, the option identifying the neutron as Chadwick's discovery is correct.***
 
• Neutrons are located in the **atomic nucleus** along with protons. The number of neutrons in an atom's nucleus determines the **isotope** of that element.
 
• The mass of a neutron is approximately **1.6749 × 10^-27 kg**, or about **1.00866 atomic mass units (amu)**. Because they lack charge, they can easily penetrate the nuclei of other atoms, making them essential for **nuclear chain reactions**.
 
• For this monumental discovery, **James Chadwick** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1935**. His work led to a deeper understanding of the atomic structure and paved the way for the development of nuclear energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electron:**

 
 
• The **electron** was the first subatomic particle to be discovered. It was identified by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** through his experiments with **Cathode Ray Tubes**.
 
• It carries a **negative electrical charge** of approximately **-1.602 × 10^-19 Coulombs** and has a very small mass (about 1/1836th of a proton).
 
 
 
• **Proton:**
 
 
• The **proton** is a positively charged particle found in the nucleus. While **Eugen Goldstein** observed canal rays in **1886**, **Ernest Rutherford** is credited with the discovery of the proton in **1917** (and naming it in **1920**) after his experiments with nitrogen nuclei.
 
• The number of protons in the nucleus defines the **atomic number** and the identity of the chemical element.
 
 
 
• **Alpha Particle:**
 
 
• An **alpha particle** consists of **two protons** and **two neutrons** bound together, making it identical to a **Helium-4 nucleus**.
 
• They are emitted during **alpha decay** of radioactive substances. **Rutherford** used these particles in his famous **Gold Foil Experiment** to discover the atomic nucleus.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Nucleus:** Discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** in **1911**. It contains almost all of the atom's mass in a very small volume, composed of **nucleons** (protons and neutrons).
 
• **Subatomic Stability:** Neutrons act as a "glue" in the nucleus; the **strong nuclear force** between neutrons and protons overcomes the electrostatic repulsion between positively charged protons, keeping the nucleus stable.
 
• **Applications:** The discovery of the neutron was crucial for the **Manhattan Project** and the subsequent creation of nuclear reactors. Neutrons are used in **neutron diffraction** to study the structure of materials and in **cancer therapy** (Boron Neutron Capture Therapy).

questions.question: Arjun Award winner Pramod Bhagat is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Para-Badminton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pramod Bhagat** is a world-renowned professional **Para-Badminton** player representing **India**. He competes primarily in the **men's singles SL3 category**, which is designated for players with impairment in one or both lower limbs and poor walking/running balance.
 
• He was honored with the prestigious **Arjuna Award** in **2019** by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of India, for his consistent and outstanding performance in the field of sports. ***Hence, the association with Para-Badminton is correct.***
 
• In **2021**, he achieved a historic milestone by winning the **Gold Medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games**. This was a landmark moment as it was the debut of badminton at the Paralympic Games.
 
• He has been a dominant force in the **BWF Para-Badminton World Championships**, securing multiple **gold medals** in both singles and doubles events over various editions, including **2015, 2019, and 2022**.
 
• As of recent rankings, he has held the **World No. 1** position in the **Para-badminton men's singles SL3** category, showcasing his longevity and skill in the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background and Early Life**:

 
 
• **Pramod Bhagat** was born on **4 June 1988** in the **Vaishali district** of **Bihar**. At the **age** of **five**, he contracted **polio**, which led to a disability in his **left leg**.
 
• Despite the physical challenges, he developed an interest in badminton after watching neighbors play, and he began competing against able-bodied players before transitioning to **para-sports** in **2006**.
 
 
 
• **Major Awards and Honors**:
 
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (2021)**: He received India's highest sporting honor following his **Paralympic** success.
 
• **Padma Shri (2022)**: He was awarded the **fourth-highest civilian award** in India for his contributions to sports.
 
• **BWF Male Para-Badminton Player of the Year**: He was nominated for and won various international accolades recognizing his technical prowess on the court.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Overview**:
 
 
• **Hockey**: This sport is associated with legends like **Major Dhyan Chand** and current stars like **Manpreet Singh** and **P.R. Sreejesh**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Para-Athletics**: This category includes track and field events. Famous Indian para-athletes include **Devendra Jhajharia** (Javelin) and **Sumit Antil**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Weightlifting**: Prominent Indian athletes in this field include **Saikhom Mirabai Chanu** (Olympic Silver medalist) and **Karnam Malleswari**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Classification in Para-Badminton**:

 
 
• The **SL3 category** (Standing Lower) requires players to play **half-court** in singles to accommodate limited mobility. **Pramod Bhagat's** tactical intelligence and net play are considered the best in this specific **classification**.
 
• Other Indian para-badminton stars include **Krishna Nagar** (SH6 category gold medalist) and **Suhas Lalinakere Yathiraj** (SL4 category silver medalist).
 
 
 
• **Training and Representation**:
 
 
• While born in Bihar, he represents the state of **Odisha** in domestic circuits and receives significant support from the **Odisha Government**, which has emerged as a major hub for sports in India.
 
• He trains at various facilities, including the **Gopi Chand Badminton Academy** and specialized centers for **para-athletes**.
